what: Pan American Silver mines silver and gold in Mexico, Peru, Bolivia, Argentina, Brazil and Canada, and holds the Escobal mine in Guatemala, which is suspended.
customers: Metal refiners and traders; silver and gold sell at world prices, so there is no customer relationship to speak of.
money: the segment it is named for
silver from Mexican and Peruvian mines
gold from the same mines and from the MAG Silver assets
moat: A spread of mines across several countries, so a problem at one does not stop the company, in an industry where primary silver mines are genuinely scarce.
risks: Revenue and profit follow metal prices, which the company does not control
Mines in Peru, Bolivia and Argentina carry political and tax risk
The Escobal mine in Guatemala has been suspended for years pending consultation with local communities
opportunities: 8.7 times earnings with a 27.1% net margin and $1.3B of free cash flow
Analysts see about 75% upside, the widest gap in precious metals coverage
Revenue grew from $1.6B to $3.6B in four years as output and metal prices rose
watch: Silver and gold production costs per ounce, and any movement on Escobal.
